keyPoints.en: Before the Western powers came, our country was stable and prosperous.
keyPoints.bm: Sebelum kuasa Barat datang, negara kita stabil dan makmur.

keyPoints.en: Stability came from the system of government, laws and foreign relations.
keyPoints.bm: Kestabilan datang daripada sistem pemerintahan, perundangan dan hubungan luar.

keyPoints.en: Prosperity came from natural resources, a good economic system and intellectual activity.
keyPoints.bm: Kemakmuran datang daripada hasil alam, sistem ekonomi yang baik dan kegiatan keintelektualan.

meaning.en: Government headed by a ruler (raja/sultan) assisted by chiefs.
meaning.bm: Pemerintahan yang diketuai raja/sultan dan dibantu pembesar.

meaning.en: Matrilineal custom of Negeri Sembilan, with rule through Undang, Lembaga and Buapak.
meaning.bm: Adat bersifat nasab ibu di Negeri Sembilan, dengan pemerintahan melalui Undang, Lembaga dan Buapak.

meaning.en: A port where goods are collected and re-exported, like Melaka.
meaning.bm: Pelabuhan tempat barang dikumpul dan dieksport semula, seperti Melaka.

meaning.en: Malay written in Arabic-based script, used for letters, laws and literature.
meaning.bm: Bahasa Melayu yang ditulis dengan huruf berasaskan Arab, digunakan untuk surat, undang-undang dan sastera.

heading.en: Stability — a. Government and social structure
heading.bm: Kestabilan — a. Sistem pemerintahan dan struktur sosial

points.en: Malay states: the Sultan at the top, helped by chiefs (e.g. the Four Chiefs in Melaka).
points.bm: Negeri Melayu: Sultan di puncak, dibantu pembesar (cth. Pembesar Empat di Melaka).

points.en: Negeri Sembilan: Yang di-Pertuan Besar → Undang → Lembaga → Buapak → anak buah.
points.bm: Negeri Sembilan: Yang di-Pertuan Besar → Undang → Lembaga → Buapak → anak buah.

points.en: Sarawak and Sabah: Brunei and Sulu appointed Pengiran and Datu; communities were led by their own chiefs.
points.bm: Sarawak dan Sabah: Brunei dan Sulu melantik Pengiran dan Datu; masyarakat dipimpin oleh ketua masing-masing.

points.en: Society: the ruling class (ruler, royal family, chiefs) and the ruled (ordinary people, slaves).
points.bm: Masyarakat: golongan pemerintah (raja, kerabat, pembesar) dan golongan diperintah (rakyat biasa, hamba).

points.en: Written laws such as Hukum Kanun Melaka, Undang-undang Laut Melaka, Undang-undang Kedah and Undang-undang 99 Perak.
points.bm: Undang-undang bertulis seperti Hukum Kanun Melaka, Undang-undang Laut Melaka, Undang-undang Kedah dan Undang-undang 99 Perak.

points.en: Customary law: Adat Temenggung and Adat Perpatih; native adat in Sarawak and Sabah.
points.bm: Undang-undang adat: Adat Temenggung dan Adat Perpatih; adat peribumi di Sarawak dan Sabah.

points.en: Diplomatic and trade ties with China, Siam, India and the Arab world kept the states safe and busy.
points.bm: Hubungan diplomatik dan perdagangan dengan China, Siam, India dan dunia Arab menjamin keselamatan dan kesibukan negeri.

heading.en: Prosperity — natural resources and their benefits

points.en: Tin and gold; forest products (rattan, resin, camphor, gaharu); sea products; birds' nests in Borneo.
points.bm: Bijih timah dan emas; hasil hutan (rotan, damar, kapur barus, gaharu); hasil laut; sarang burung di Borneo.

points.en: These attracted traders and brought wealth to the rulers and people.
points.bm: Hasil ini menarik pedagang dan membawa kekayaan kepada pemerintah dan rakyat.

points.en: Trade and ports: Melaka was a great entrepôt; other ports included Kuala Kedah and Brunei.
points.bm: Perdagangan dan pelabuhan: Melaka pelabuhan entrepot agung; pelabuhan lain termasuk Kuala Kedah dan Brunei.

points.en: Weights and measures (gantang, cupak, kati, tahil), currency (e.g. tin and gold coins) and taxes on trade.
points.bm: Timbang, sukat dan ukur (gantang, cupak, kati, tahil), mata wang (cth. syiling timah dan emas) serta cukai perdagangan.

points.en: Non-formal education at home, at the palace and with religious teachers; formal education in pondok schools.
points.bm: Pendidikan tidak formal di rumah, istana dan dengan guru agama; pendidikan formal di sekolah pondok.

points.en: Malay was the lingua franca; Jawi script was widely used; literature such as Sejarah Melayu and Hikayat Hang Tuah.
points.bm: Bahasa Melayu lingua franca; tulisan Jawi digunakan dengan meluas; karya sastera seperti Sejarah Melayu dan Hikayat Hang Tuah.

alt.en: Replica of the Melaka Sultanate palace — a reminder of the kingdom's greatness before 1511.
alt.bm: Replika istana Kesultanan Melayu Melaka — peringatan kegemilangan kerajaan sebelum 1511.

caption.en: Replica of the Melaka Sultanate palace — a reminder of the kingdom's greatness before 1511.
caption.bm: Replika istana Kesultanan Melayu Melaka — peringatan kegemilangan kerajaan sebelum 1511.

question.en: Explain TWO reasons why the Malay kingdoms were stable before the Western powers came.
question.bm: Jelaskan DUA sebab kerajaan Melayu stabil sebelum kedatangan kuasa Barat.

answer.en: (1) An organised system of government — a ruler helped by chiefs with clear duties. (2) Written and customary laws kept order and justice.
answer.bm: (1) Sistem pemerintahan yang tersusun — raja dibantu pembesar yang mempunyai tugas jelas. (2) Undang-undang bertulis dan adat menjaga ketenteraman dan keadilan.

keyPoints.en: Western powers came for different reasons in different centuries.
keyPoints.bm: Kuasa Barat datang atas sebab yang berbeza pada abad yang berbeza.

keyPoints.en: 16th century: luxury goods (spices), Melaka as a collecting centre and port of call, and spreading Christianity ("Gold, Glory, Gospel").
keyPoints.bm: Abad ke-16: barangan mewah (rempah), Melaka sebagai pusat pengumpulan barang dan pelabuhan persinggahan, serta menyebarkan agama Kristian ("Gold, Glory, Gospel").

keyPoints.en: 17th–18th centuries: the Industrial Revolution created demand for raw materials and markets.
keyPoints.bm: Abad ke-17 hingga ke-18: Revolusi Perindustrian mewujudkan permintaan bahan mentah dan pasaran.

keyPoints.en: 19th–20th centuries: the motorcar and canning industries, fertile land, the Suez Canal, steamships, the telegraph, rivalry and "the White Man's Burden".
keyPoints.bm: Abad ke-19 hingga ke-20: industri kereta dan mengetin, tanah yang subur, Terusan Suez, kapal wap, telegraf, persaingan dan "Beban Orang Putih".

meaning.en: Gold (wealth), Glory (power and fame), Gospel (spreading Christianity).
meaning.bm: Gold (kekayaan), Glory (kuasa dan kemasyhuran), Gospel (menyebarkan agama Kristian).

meaning.en: Change from hand-made to machine production, starting in Britain in the 18th century.
meaning.bm: Perubahan daripada pengeluaran tangan kepada mesin, bermula di Britain pada abad ke-18.

meaning.en: Opened in 1869; made the voyage from Europe to Asia much shorter.
meaning.bm: Dibuka pada 1869; memendekkan pelayaran dari Eropah ke Asia.

meaning.en: The Western claim that they had a duty to "civilise" other peoples — used to justify colonisation.
meaning.bm: Dakwaan Barat bahawa mereka bertanggungjawab "memperadabkan" bangsa lain — digunakan untuk menghalalkan penjajahan.

points.en: Luxury goods: spices, silk and porcelain fetched very high prices in Europe.
points.bm: Barangan mewah: rempah, sutera dan tembikar mendapat harga yang sangat tinggi di Eropah.

points.en: Collecting centre and port of call: Melaka gathered goods from East and West and was a stop on the monsoon routes.
points.bm: Pusat pengumpulan barang dan pelabuhan persinggahan: Melaka mengumpul barang dari Timur dan Barat serta menjadi persinggahan laluan monsun.

points.en: Religion: the Portuguese wanted to spread Christianity and weaken Muslim traders.
points.bm: Agama: Portugis mahu menyebarkan agama Kristian dan melemahkan pedagang Islam.

points.en: The Industrial Revolution: factories needed raw materials (tin) and new markets for their products.
points.bm: Revolusi Perindustrian: kilang memerlukan bahan mentah (bijih timah) dan pasaran baharu untuk keluarannya.

points.en: Motorcar industry → demand for rubber tyres; canning industry → demand for tin.
points.bm: Industri kereta → permintaan tayar getah; industri mengetin → permintaan bijih timah.

points.en: Fertile land and rich resources suited plantations and mines.
points.bm: Tanah yang subur dan hasil bumi yang kaya sesuai untuk ladang dan lombong.

points.en: Suez Canal (1869), steamships and the telegraph made travel and communication faster.
points.bm: Terusan Suez (1869), kapal wap dan telegraf mempercepat perjalanan dan perhubungan.

points.en: Rivalry between Western powers and the "White Man's Burden" idea.
points.bm: Persaingan antara kuasa Barat dan idea "Beban Orang Putih".

question.en: How did the motorcar industry affect our country?
question.bm: Bagaimanakah industri kereta memberi kesan kepada negara kita?

answer.en: Cars needed rubber tyres, so demand for rubber soared in the early 1900s and the British opened huge rubber estates here.
answer.bm: Kereta memerlukan tayar getah, maka permintaan getah melonjak pada awal 1900-an dan British membuka ladang getah yang besar di sini.

tip.en: Sort factors by century: 16th — 3G; 17th–18th — Industrial Revolution; 19th–20th — technology and industry.
tip.bm: Susun faktor mengikut abad: ke-16 — 3G; ke-17–18 — Revolusi Perindustrian; ke-19–20 — teknologi dan industri.

keyPoints.en: The Portuguese, Dutch and British competed for colonies in the Malay world.
keyPoints.bm: Portugis, Belanda dan British bersaing mendapatkan tanah jajahan di Alam Melayu.

keyPoints.en: The Portuguese captured Melaka in 1511 under Afonso de Albuquerque.
keyPoints.bm: Portugis menawan Melaka pada 1511 di bawah Afonso de Albuquerque.

keyPoints.en: The Dutch, allied with Johor, took Melaka from the Portuguese in 1641.
keyPoints.bm: Belanda, bersekutu dengan Johor, merampas Melaka daripada Portugis pada 1641.

keyPoints.en: The British took Penang (1786) and Singapore (1819); the rivalry with the Dutch was settled by the London Treaty of 1824.
keyPoints.bm: British mengambil Pulau Pinang (1786) dan Singapura (1819); persaingan dengan Belanda diselesaikan melalui Perjanjian London 1824.

meaning.en: A territory controlled by a foreign power.
Dutch East India Company — ran Dutch trade and colonies in the East.
meaning.bm: Syarikat Hindia Timur Belanda — menguruskan perdagangan dan tanah jajahan Belanda di Timur.

meaning.en: British East India Company (Syarikat Hindia Timur Inggeris).

points.en: After 1511, Johor and Acheh repeatedly attacked Portuguese Melaka.
points.bm: Selepas 1511, Johor dan Acheh berulang kali menyerang Melaka Portugis.

points.en: The Dutch built their centre at Batavia and joined Johor to defeat the Portuguese in 1641.
points.bm: Belanda membina pusatnya di Batavia dan bergabung dengan Johor untuk mengalahkan Portugis pada 1641.

points.en: In the late 1700s the British needed a base in the region for their India–China trade.
points.bm: Pada akhir 1700-an British memerlukan pangkalan di rantau ini untuk perdagangan India–China.

points.en: British–Dutch rivalry over trade and influence ended with the London Treaty (1824).
points.bm: Persaingan British–Belanda tentang perdagangan dan pengaruh berakhir dengan Perjanjian London (1824).

event.en: London Treaty divides the Malay world.

question.en: Why did the Dutch help Johor attack Portuguese Melaka?
question.bm: Mengapakah Belanda membantu Johor menyerang Melaka Portugis?

answer.en: Both wanted to remove the Portuguese: Johor to regain its lost lands and trade, and the Dutch to control the spice trade and the Strait of Melaka.
answer.bm: Kedua-duanya mahu menyingkirkan Portugis: Johor untuk mendapatkan semula wilayah dan perdagangannya, dan Belanda untuk menguasai perdagangan rempah dan Selat Melaka.

keyPoints.en: The Dutch and the British used different strategies to control our country.
keyPoints.bm: Belanda dan British menggunakan strategi berbeza untuk menguasai negara kita.

keyPoints.en: Dutch: physical attack, agreements (e.g. trade monopolies) and alliances.
keyPoints.bm: Belanda: serangan fizikal, perjanjian (cth. monopoli perdagangan) dan pakatan.

keyPoints.en: British: manipulation, trickery, alliances, threats and pressure, agreements, leases and physical attack.
keyPoints.bm: British: manipulasi, tipu helah, pakatan, ugutan dan desakan, perjanjian, pajakan dan serangan fizikal.

meaning.en: Sole right to trade a product, e.g. the Dutch tin monopoly.
meaning.bm: Hak tunggal memperdagangkan sesuatu barang, cth. monopoli bijih timah Belanda.

meaning.en: Exploiting local quarrels, e.g. succession disputes, for one's own gain.
meaning.bm: Mengeksploitasi pertelingkahan tempatan, cth. perebutan takhta, untuk kepentingan sendiri.

meaning.en: Renting land for a payment, e.g. Penang and Seberang Perai from Kedah.
meaning.bm: Menyewa tanah dengan bayaran, cth. Pulau Pinang dan Seberang Perai daripada Kedah.

points.en: Physical attack: the siege of Melaka with Johor (1641).
points.bm: Serangan fizikal: pengepungan Melaka bersama Johor (1641).

points.en: Agreements: treaties with local rulers to buy tin only from the Dutch.
points.bm: Perjanjian: perjanjian dengan pemerintah tempatan untuk menjual bijih timah kepada Belanda sahaja.

points.en: Alliances: working with Johor against the Portuguese.
points.bm: Pakatan: bekerjasama dengan Johor menentang Portugis.

points.en: Manipulation and trickery: e.g. Francis Light promised Kedah protection; Raffles recognised Tengku Hussein as Sultan to obtain Singapore.
points.bm: Manipulasi dan tipu helah: cth. Francis Light menjanjikan perlindungan kepada Kedah; Raffles mengiktiraf Tengku Hussein sebagai Sultan untuk mendapatkan Singapura.

points.en: Threats and pressure on rulers to accept British officers (e.g. Pahang).
points.bm: Ugutan dan desakan supaya raja menerima pegawai British (cth. Pahang).

points.en: Agreements and leases: e.g. Pangkor Treaty (1874); Penang and Seberang Perai leased from Kedah.
points.bm: Perjanjian dan pajakan: cth. Perjanjian Pangkor (1874); Pulau Pinang dan Seberang Perai dipajak daripada Kedah.

points.en: Physical attack: e.g. the Naning War (1831–1832).
points.bm: Serangan fizikal: cth. Perang Naning (1831–1832).

question.en: Compare the strategies of the Dutch and the British.

answer.en: The Dutch relied more on force and trade monopolies; the British mostly used diplomacy — manipulation, agreements and leases — and used force only when needed.
answer.bm: Belanda lebih bergantung pada kekerasan dan monopoli perdagangan; British kebanyakannya menggunakan diplomasi — manipulasi, perjanjian dan pajakan — dan menggunakan kekerasan apabila perlu sahaja.
